newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China troops welcome in HK bar, but can they pay?
newsitem.headline: China troops welcome in HK bar, but can they pay?

text.p: Chinese soldiers in Hong Kong will be able to tread where no British troops can set foot -- into one of the territory's trendier bars.

An advance unit of 40 People's Liberation Army (PLA) soldiers arrived in the territory on Monday to prepare the way for the garrison that will take over from the British military when Hong Kong reverts to Chinese rule at midnight on June 30.

"With the PLA, we'll give them a fair shake and we'd let them come through, and they would be welcome to Joe Bananas," Billy Dock, business development director at the popular night spot in the Wanchai entertainment district, said on Tuesday.
"But again, if things didn't work out and they got too boistrous, we'd have to install that rule again," he told Reuters.
Dock said Joe Bananas banned military personnel 11 years ago although officers are allowed in.
However, the chances of the PLA taking up the offer are slim.
A locally-brewed beer at popular bars sells for about HK$45 (US$5.80) -- while an average PLA foot soldier gets paid just 40 yuan (US$4.80) per month.
The garrison commander, Major-General Liu Zhenwu, will be paid 1,200 yuan (US$145) a month -- less than the minimum wage of HK$3,860 for foreign domestic servants.
But PLA soldiers may never have to worry about pooling their change outside the bars of Wanchai.
Liu told pro-China newspapers in Hong Kong last year that soldiers would need a good reason to leave the barracks and would have to leave and return as a unit and under escort.
